title: I asked Claude & ChatGPT both for an idea for a space game.. the result baffled me
author: AddictedToTech
selftext:
The premise is practically 1:1 the same. A reminder how these models are pretty much equal in capability and originality.

What are your tips for ideating with LLM and how do you get original ideas?

comments.author: Existing-Strength-21
comments.body:
Get original ideas by turning it in to more of a dialog. I usually start by giving it a 3 or 4 paragraph rambling rant kn what im trying to achieve. Then I instruct it to rephrase my concept back to me so I know it understands and I will have it ask me a number of clarifying questions to better understand the point. 

The more of a dialog back and forth with the LLM, the deeper you're going to get in to the latent code space and you won't land in the same or similar spaces as everyone else.

replies.author: SafePostsAccount
replies.body: Gibberish to effectively throw some randomization into the llms predictions

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body: I'm willing to bet people are just going to copy-paste that exact quasi-random-seed and be surprised they'll get similar results.

comments.author: RogueStargun
comments.body: Changing the temperature settings should give you more diverse or more generic outputs

comments.author: tsfreaks
comments.body:
LLMs are  good and regurgitating well known things and generally bad at original ideas. You provide the original ideas and use LLMs to back fill. 

When technique is to start super narrow. I want design a space adventure. I don't know where to start so let's start with a freckle on the nose of my main character. Prompt me with questions to get the design going.

comments.author: ELPascalito
comments.body: For the last time, LLMs are deterministic, and a very vague question like yours will always yield similar results, because the "generic question" matches too many generic tokens from answers that the LLM was trained on, and since they're both trained on the internet, they'll both give you the generic response! Try being more specific, or try raising the temperature of the LLM so it'll respond in aore broad and "creative" way! Best of luck!

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body: I can only recommend taking a page out of solo roleplaying systems and randomly generating seed words to throw at the LLM. LLMs are also decent at generating random tables that you can then use for inspiration or to ask the LLM to loop back and detail things further.

comments.author: LopsidedLobster2100
comments.body: damn it all looks plagiarized. terran, really? this is a thinking machine?

comments.author: Environmental-Meal72
comments.body: You can get original ideas by closing the GPT window, taking a deep breath and using your brain. Feed your imagination and subconcious

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: Sounds like a fun game tho.

comments.author: bitgardener
comments.body: Good reminder that the only thing that will make a solo game dev project stand out is the creativity behind it, and if you offload that to an LLM… well, you tell me if this is “creative”, if they both just suggest the same generic concepts.

comments.author: Pretend-Park6473
comments.body:
\>how do you get original ideas

they kind of pop up in my head

comments.author: FridgeBaron
comments.body:
I have an idea then I use an LLM like I'm explaining the idea to someone. They ask questions and it forces me to figure it out. I do also sometimes just ramble at it with ideas to see what suggestions it has, take the ones you like and repeat.

Just treat it like actual brainstorming, don't latch on to the first idea, see what you can get.
